articles.search_term: ("हीट एक्शन प्लान" OR "गर्मी से राहत" OR चेतावनी OR "रेड अलर्ट" OR "ऑरेंज अलर्ट" OR "येलो अलर्ट" OR एडवाइजरी OR "राहत सामग्री" OR "राहत शिविर" OR मुआवजा) Chhattisgarh
articles.full_text:
खैरागढ़। CG NEWS: जिले के ग्राम पंचायत जुरलाकला के आश्रित ग्राम रीवागहन में 20 मार्च 2026 की देर रात किसान उत्तम वर्मा के कोठार में रखे पैरावट में अचानक आग लग गई। आग देखते ही देखते फैल गई और कोठार में खड़ी मोटरसाइकिल, छह कट्टा बटरी तथा घर का काफी हिस्सा जलकर राख हो गया। आग की चपेट में आने से दो गायें भी गंभीर रूप से झुलस गईं। इलाज के दौरान दोनों ने दम तोड़ दिया।
घटना के समय उत्तम वर्मा का परिवार घर में सो रहा था। आसपास के लोगों ने आवाज लगाकर उन्हें जगाया। इसके बाद डायल-112 और फायर ब्रिगेड को सूचना दी गई। काफी मशक्कत के बाद आग पर काबू पाया गया। किसान के मुताबिक हादसे में करीब दो लाख रुपये का नुकसान हुआ है।
उत्तम वर्मा ने खैरागढ़ थाने में एफआईआर दर्ज कराई है, लेकिन आग लगने के कारणों का अब तक पता नहीं चल सका है। घटना के बाद से किसान मुआवजे की मांग को लेकर कलेक्टर और तहसील कार्यालय के चक्कर काट रहा है। उन्होंने प्रशासन से उचित क्षतिपूर्ति जल्द दिलाने की मांग की है।

Rajasthan heat breaks 15-year record:Jaisalmer-Barmer cross 43°C; rain likely across state next week
Record-breaking heat continued in Rajasthan for the second consecutive day. The daytime temperature crossed 43°C in Jaisalmer and Barmer, reaching levels not seen in September over the last 15 years. Mercury also crossed 40°C in Jodhpur, Churu, and Bikaner.
Weather experts noted that similar heat is expected in the state over the next two to three days, while under the influence of a Western Disturbance, thunderstorms and rain are likely in parts of Eastern Rajasthan next week.
During the past 24 hours, Barmer and Jaisalmer experienced the most intense heat. On Thursday, the maximum daytime temperature was recorded at 43.6°C in Barmer and 43.2°C in Jaisalmer. Along with the heat, hot winds blew through the western districts of Rajasthan during the day.
Jodhpur recorded its hottest day in 11 years on Thursday; prior to this, the maximum temperature here was recorded at 40.6°C in 2016. Meanwhile, temperatures in Barmer had never reached 43°C in the month of September over the last 11 years.
Why the Heat Suddenly Increased
Radheshyam Sharma, Director of the Meteorological Centre, Jaipur, explained that after the monsoon retreats, wind directions in the atmosphere change and an anti-cyclone forms. Due to the formation of this anti-cyclonic system, hot winds coming from the western direction circulate clockwise within Rajasthan and its surrounding areas. The director noted that similar weather conditions are expected to prevail across Rajasthan for the next two to three days.
Intense Heat Recorded Here as Well
Meanwhile, maximum temperatures were recorded at 41.7°C in Jodhpur, 41.6°C in Bikaner, 40.5°C in Churu, 40.3°C in Nagaur, 39.5°C in Fatehpur, 39.2°C in Pilani, and 39.4°C in Jalore. In these cities too, people are sweltering through both the days and nights.

Monsoon Retreats From All Cities Except Kota-Udaipur Divisions
Today in Rajasthan, the monsoon has withdrawn from all parts of the Jaipur, Ajmer, Bharatpur, and Jodhpur divisions. Meanwhile, the monsoon remains active in areas of the Kota and Udaipur divisions, with the likelihood that it will retreat from these regions as well in 2–3 days.
Weather May Change From 27 September
The Meteorological Centre, Jaipur, has indicated the possibility of a weather shift in Rajasthan due to the combined influence of a Western Disturbance and a cyclonic system formed in the Bay of Bengal. Thunderstorms and rain are likely in the eastern Rajasthan districts of Sikar, Jhunjhunu, Jaipur, Alwar, Dausa, Bharatpur, Dholpur, Karauli, and Sawai Madhopur starting 27 September, and in Alwar, Dausa, Bharatpur, Dholpur, Karauli, and Sawai Madhopur on 28 September.
Weather Condition in Major Districts of Rajasthan
In the state capital, Jaipur, daytime temperatures fell by nearly 2 degrees on Thursday, but it offered little relief from the heat. The maximum daytime temperature here was recorded at 34.6°C. Bright sunshine prevailed in Jaipur from morning till late evening alongside mild humidity.
In Kota on Thursday, the effect of heat and humidity persisted. High intensity of sunshine continued throughout the day. The mercury dipped by 1 degree. The maximum temperature reached 34.4°C, while the minimum temperature was recorded at 25.2°C. No rainfall occurred until 5:30 PM.
In Udaipur on Thursday, people were troubled by the heat and humidity. The daytime temperature saw an increase of 1°C. According to the Meteorological Department, the daytime temperature reached 37°C, compared to 36°C recorded a day earlier.
In Sikar on Thursday, bright sunshine and humid weather prevailed throughout the day. In the evening, light clouds gathered in some areas. Heat has been continuously rising in Sikar over the last 4 days. Due to strong sunlight during the day, a steady rise in temperature is being observed. At the Fatehpur Weather Station in Sikar, the maximum daytime temperature was recorded at 39.5°C, while the minimum temperature stood at 20.7°C.
In Jodhpur, the impact of heat persists even in the final days of September. Bright sunshine prevailed during the day on Thursday. The maximum temperature was recorded at 41.7°C, which was 5.8 degrees above normal. The minimum temperature was recorded at 25.8°C, standing 1.8 degrees above normal. According to the Meteorological Department, there is no likelihood of rain in the coming few days.
In Alwar district, the weather remained clear throughout the day on Thursday with bright sunshine. Due to this, the daytime temperature reached 36.6°C. While the impact of the heat was felt, there is every possibility of temperatures dropping in the coming days.
In Ajmer, the impact of the heat continued throughout the day on Thursday. Bright sunshine since the morning left people troubled by humidity and scorching heat. The maximum daytime temperature was recorded at 37.5°C, while the minimum temperature stood at 22.6°C.

As someone who lives in India, I know a thing (or ten) about intense heat. This summer is proving to be particularly hot, going up to 107 degrees F (42 degrees Celsius) in my city. Other parts of the world are also experiencing heatwaves, and if you're going out on vacation or just need a way to stay cool while outdoors, there's a product for you.
Accessory brand Torras makes wearable air conditioners, and the Coolify Cyber Fold does a great job controlling your microclimate — the immediate vicinity around you. It's designed to cool up to 50 degrees F and provides cool airflow of 3m/s, and you know what? It actually works. I tested it for the last two months, and even on days when it was 104 degrees out (40 deg C), it made a legitimate difference. The Cyber Fold is the costliest model in the Coolify range, and it costs $279. If you need an affordable alternative, the Coolify 2S Pro is a good option at $199, and the Coolify Air is just $129 right now.
The Coolify Cyber Fold has much better build quality than other wearable ACs, and it uses Peltier cooling tech in conjunction with fans to ensure you stay cool outdoors. There are eight vents around the product that blow air, and you get decent coverage around your face and neck.
Obviously, the design means it will stand out when you're wearing it in public — there's no getting around that. But I will admit that it isn't as bulky or unwieldy as it looks, and I didn't notice the heft after a day or two of regular use. The best part about the Cyber Fold is that it's effective even on days where it's over 100 degrees F, and the cooling pads around your neck make a huge difference.
The built-in battery doesn't quite last all day, but it's good enough for a few hours of use on full blast. You can eke out better battery life by switching to efficient cooling, and unless it's over 100 degrees outside, you won't need to crank up the cooling all the way.
It is a niche product, but it's one that made a decent amount of difference in the summer months, and if you're interested in trying out a wearable AC, the Cyber Fold is the one I'd recommend.

articles.title: Cyclone Arnab Update: Heavy Rain Lashes Odisha & Andhra Pradesh As Red Alert Remains In Place - curlytales.com

articles.full_text:
Odisha and Andhra Pradesh are witnessing another spell of intense rainfall. A deep depression that crossed the North Andhra Pradesh-South Odisha coast near Kalingapatnam has continued to bring heavy rainfall, waterlogging and disruptions across the region. While the system is now expected to weaken gradually, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has warned of more rain in several areas. Scroll on to know more about this.
What Is The Weather Situation In Odisha & Andhra Pradesh?
The weather system crossed the coast in the early hours of September 24 and moved further inland. According to the IMD, it is expected to weaken gradually from a deep depression into a depression. However, its impact is still being felt across parts of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh, with heavy rain, thunderstorms and strong winds reported in several areas.
According to The Hindu, the IMD has issued a red warning for Koraput, Nabarangpur and Kalahandi in Odisha for September 25. Malkangiri, Nuapada, Kandhamal, Rayagada, Ganjam and Gajapati are among the districts under an orange warning.
Several parts of Odisha have witnessed waterlogging and flooding following the intense spell of rain. Landslides have also affected transport in some areas, with train services disrupted between Maligura and Chhatariput stations.
In Andhra Pradesh, the north coastal region has also received heavy rainfall, with roads and fields inundated and trees uprooted in some areas.
For Coastal Andhra Pradesh, the IMD has forecast heavy rain on September 25, along with thunderstorms, lightning and strong surface winds. Similar thunderstorm and strong-wind warnings extend into the following days.
Odisha is also expected to see more rain, particularly across southern and interior districts. The IMD’s latest bulletins indicate that the system will gradually weaken as it moves further inland, but rainfall remains the immediate concern.
While the weather system was widely referred to as “Cyclone Arnab” in some reports, the IMD tracked it as a deep depression rather than a cyclonic storm. “Arnab” is the next name on the North Indian Ocean cyclone naming list; a system receives that name only after reaching the required cyclone intensity.
For now, the focus remains on the heavy rain, flooding and landslide risks across affected areas as the system weakens.
With red and orange warnings still in place in parts of Odisha, residents are advised to follow local administration and IMD updates and avoid unnecessary travel.
Is Cyclone Arnab hitting Odisha and Andhra Pradesh?
No, despite reports referring to “Arnab”, the IMD clarified that the system did not intensify into a cyclonic storm. It remained a deep depression after crossing the Andhra Pradesh coast.
Why was the weather system called Arnab?
“Arnab” is the name that would have been assigned to the system if it had intensified into a cyclonic storm. The name was contributed by Bangladesh and means “ocean” in Bengali.
Where did the deep depression make landfall?
The system crossed the coast near Kalingapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, between late September 23 and early September 24, with maximum sustained winds of around 55–65 kmph and gusts up to 75 kmph.
